description: Perch v2 as a CPCP surface: sized slices, the freeze ladder, the orphan ledger, and the outward signal. Seven operations on BACK.

seam.because: Perch is a PROJECTION on BACK via RailsCpcp.project, not a container and not a ROLE. ADR 0056 makes BACK and BACKJOB the writers, and a second writer for one domain is the fork that doctrine exists to prevent.

not.effect_gate: BACK is the gate (ADR 0056). No perch.effect.execute, no executor, no credential reachable from this surface.
not.effect_ledger: The operation journal is admission truth (ADR 0052). This surface reports what an approval was BOUND TO; what happened under it is the journal's, and a perch.effect.proposed/decided/executed would be a second ledger.
not.signatures: No JWS crosses this wire. The binding is kept so invalidation is computable without holding the credential that would make it enforceable here.
not.ranking: No perch.slice.rank. P2 puts ranking outside Perch; the surface passes rank_together as a constraint and never a position.

identity.source: Authorization: Bearer, read from the request header by BPMN_BEARER
identity.never: actor_id is NOT a declared wire param on any operation. A supplied actor_id is reconciled against the bearer and refused on mismatch; it can never establish identity.
identity.roster: BPMN_REVIEW_ACTORS, fail-closed: absent, empty or unparseable is a refusal, never an anonymous caller.

idempotency.rule: Every PUSH declares operationId. Replay returns the first result and is counted as traffic, not as a second admission.

operations.name: perch.slice.size
operations.returns: Findings per slice, each tiered floor | price | symptom.
operations.because: Floor failures (T1–T5) are refusals because a piece below the floor cannot be managed around. Price findings (T6) and symptoms (T7, T8) are RECORDED, not refused — a symptom that blocks is a symptom people route around.

operations.name: perch.slice.status
operations.summary: Computed gate / group / signal triple; pending is not zero
operations.returns: gate_passed_at, released_at, ready_waiting_on_group, done, advisory, needs_envelope, stale_approvals, signals.
operations.because: done is computed from released + instrumented + reporting and is never a column. ready_waiting_on_group is a member that finished early — it is not done, and §12.2 counts released slices only.

operations.name: perch.slice.restate
operations.summary: T4: bound Actor restates Aim and Receiver
operations.because: T4 is a non-engineering owner restating the aim in their own words. It is identity-bound because the restatement is evidence about WHO understood the slice; an anonymous restatement is not the test.

operations.name: perch.freeze.cascade
operations.summary: Current cascade cost of a freeze; not the stored climb record
operations.returns: cost_shown_at_climb (the record), price_now (the query), and the current cascade.
operations.because: F5 prices a change before it is accepted. Two costs, two objects: the record is what the climber accepted and is never recomputed; the price is what a change would cost now. Returning only the first is how F5 becomes a memo. Magnitudes are not estimated — this surface holds no training history or signer roster, so counts and bearers are measured and hours are not.

operations.name: perch.orphan.open
operations.summary: Open orphan-ledger entries and their parties
operations.returns: Entries with unmet_obligations, managed, questionable, derived convergence, and parties.
operations.because: P3: orphaning is a price payable only if the liability is written down AND managed. unmet_obligations is a list rather than a verdict — 'what does this still owe' is answerable and 'is this ok' is not the question. A boundary_to_question is flagged separately because §11.1 says it is escalated, not scheduled.

operations.name: perch.signal.report
operations.summary: Readings with maturity; pending is not a fail
operations.returns: signal_state, done, and per reading: measured, observed_at, window_closes_at.
operations.because: Three states, closed: not_instrumented, pending, reporting. A null value inside an open window is PENDING, never an aim unmet — reading it as failure kills a released slice inside its own measurement window. Only an outward reading can close a window; an inward verdict is necessary and never sufficient (§12.1).

operations.name: perch.release
operations.returns: group_key, released_at, member count, and the binding actor.
operations.because: Release groups go together or not at all. A slice cannot mint its own release; the group writes every member in one transaction and refuses if any member has not passed its gate.

refusal_vocabulary.shape: { ok: false, reason, because }. never-raise. The reason is the thing a caller branches on; a free-text reason is how a contract turns into string matching.

seam.unknown_operation: a method this surface does not serve
seam.no_such_slice: the slice_key resolves to nothing in that use case
seam.perch_tables_missing: the perch_ schema is not migrated here. Fail closed: absent tables are not an empty ledger

identity.actor_cid_unbound: the bearer is bound to an actor_id but no actor_cid, and the seam journals a CID. Bind one in the operator roster rather than letting the caller supply it
identity.actor_override_refused: a supplied actor_id or actorCid disagrees with the bearer. Neither side silently wins
identity.review_actors_actor_missing: a roster entry names nobody: neither an integer actor_id nor an actor_cid. A token that resolves to no actor cannot attribute anything
identity.review_actors_missing: the actor roster is absent or empty. Fail closed, never anonymous
identity.review_actors_token_collision: one token maps to two actors, so a review cannot be attributed to either
identity.review_actors_unparseable: the roster is not a JSON object the binding can read
identity.review_unauthenticated: no bearer, or a bearer the roster does not know, on an identity-bound operation

domain.note: Every reason this surface can return from the domain is in that closed set. A reason outside it is a bug in the gem, not a new case.

contract.note: This fragment is CHECKED against the live projection, not maintained beside it. check_perch_contract.py compares every name, direction and param here with what the initializer declares, and every refusal named here with the gem's closed set. A contract nobody verifies is a memo, which is the failure this repo has already paid for once in CANONICAL.md.
